# Music status: every piece considered for the game

One living page for the music: every work on the *Legend of the Galactic Heroes* (LOGH) list, every other piece in the game's catalogue, and any piece the user wants considered. The facts that come from the repository (catalogue numbers, instruments, treatment, sources, where each piece is heard) are derived by `tools/music_status.py`; what a person knows (the LOGH rows, notes on a piece) is in `data/music/status-notes.json`. To add a piece, see [Adding a piece](#adding-a-piece).

The catalogue has 117 pieces (numbers 0–116, their positions in `MUSIC_PIECES`): 63 of them are pieces of LOGH works and 54 are not.

## Reading this page

**Status** (one of):

- **in the game**: the piece (or every movement LOGH uses) is in the catalogue, with its catalogue number(s);
- **partly**: some movements or an excerpt are in the game; the notes say which are not;
- **source found, not arranged**: a note source that passes our rules exists (a Mutopia public-domain edition, a staged CC0 PDMX row) but nothing is in the catalogue yet;
- **wanted**: no public-domain source found yet (or not yet researched; the note says which);
- **blocked**: something stops it. Either the work is not public domain and needs the user's explicit approval, or only a public-domain *scan* exists (an IMSLP edition), so our own transcription waits on the OMR reader. A wider PDMX search has not been done for the scan-only works, so some of them may move to "source found";
- **not planned**: cannot be identified as one work, or deliberately left out;
- **requested**: added by the user for consideration, not yet researched.

**The rule for music.** The user's ruling (2026-11-20): anything public domain is fine; anything that is not needs their explicit approval. For a composition that means public domain in the US (published 1930 or earlier, in 2026) and in the EU (every author died 70 or more years ago). The note data must come from a CC0 or public-domain transcription (Mutopia "Public Domain", a PDMX/MuseScore row marked CC0 with no licence conflict) or from our own transcription of a public-domain scan, which is dedicated to CC0 (data/music/SOURCES.md has every record and permission). Nothing here is a recording.

**Instruments.** "In the game" is read from the packed events: the synthesizer's timbres, with a share of the notes; a timbre under 2% of the notes is called a few notes. "Source file" is the General MIDI program names of the source file's tracks (percussion as such); Mutopia's LilyPond files often carry a default piano program whatever the score's instruments, so the "scoring" line says what the work and the source really are. The packer maps programs to timbres: pianos to piano; harp; accordions; choir and voices to choir; guitars, banjo and sitars to banjo; basses to bass; timpani; strings to strings; brass to brass; clarinets and all saxophones to clarinet; oboe and English horn to oboe; bassoon; flutes, piccolo and recorders to flute; anything else to strings. The *island pluck* ("bouzouki") stands for the bouzouki, mandolin and guitar, and the harp model also stands for the guitar in several arrangements. The piano follows the venue: the concert grand on the classical programme, the honky-tonk upright at the bar and on the popular and dance programmes ([docs/music-orchestra.md](music-orchestra.md)).

**Treatment** is the performance given on top of the notes ([docs/music-performance.md](music-performance.md)): the generic phrase rules, the automatic part balance (tools/music_part_balance.py), the level in the mix, grace notes (tools/music_grace.py), tempo against the score (tools/music_tempo.py), plus anything done by hand. The level is 1 unless shown: measured to a common loudness by tools/music_level.py (levels.json) or set by ear. Voice stealing (which note gives way when the 64 voices are all busy: `music_steal` in src/music_synth.jo) is one rule for every piece; no piece sets its own. No piece is transposed, and the packer cuts nothing except the Greek songs' introductions and interludes.

**Catalogue numbers** are positions in `MUSIC_PIECES` (data/music/catalogue.json), the numbers the radio, the band and the title use. The `L` numbers are positions in the LOGH list (from 1, in the list's order: composer, then work).

## The LOGH list, work by work

Every one of the 211 works on the user's list (the original 110-episode OVA, the films *My Conquest Is the Sea of Stars* and *Overture to a New War*, and *Gaiden*; not *Die Neue These*). One row per work; "Used in LOGH" names the movements the earlier research (a scrape of Gineipaedia's per-episode music sections) found, with the films' cues from the list; the list is a work-level catalogue, not a cue sheet. *Golden Wings* has no pre-existing classical cue. The list's "entries requiring closer identification" are folded into the rows they concern (the Shostakovich "Symphony No. 2, III" is not counted).

## Where the music is heard

### Radio rounds

Each station plays its programme's round of pieces, one after another, each heard whole from its start, on the saved world clock (`radio_pool`, `radio_cue` in src/radio_synth.jo); every station joins the round at its own place (an offset of 1913 s times its number), so two stations on the same round are not on the same piece. The programme clock takes the news, weather, editorial and quiz minutes from the music ([docs/radio.md](radio.md)); hours are local time (the world's minute 0 is 09:30). The Blue Lantern and the dance-hour blocks turn between foxtrot, tango and waltz every half hour, so each of those three rounds airs a third of the time there. The first six stations are on the air by their own rules; the later stations by their blocks (`radio_blocks` in src/radio.jo).

The island round is also Archipelago Radio's and Radio Dawn's: Ikariotikos and the first eight Greek songs. The Café round is the lighter mixed list of Radio Porto Vecchio's mornings, Radio Mandolinata's mornings and the Meltemi Weather Wireless's tunes; the Café Aman round adds the two Hotel Ancora Greek songs. The spoken stations' news and weather are read aloud by the announcer, not music; the Aegean Maritime Service plays no music (Morse, weather and shipping).

### The hotel band

The Hotel Ancora's band plays in the evening, from 19:00 to 23:30 (local time), the numbers of its set in order, round again until it stops, 7 seconds between numbers, in the open air of the terrace (the upright piano always). Its request list is the whole set: a number asked of the band (and tipped) is played next, then the evening goes on where it was. A number plays when its players are in their places (`src/band_life.jo`). The set (`BAR_SET` in src/bar_band.jo):

| Order | Piece | Line-up | Evenings | Sung |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Gymnopedie No. 1](#p7) | piano alone, the tune on the piano | every evening |  |
| 2 | [Ave Maria (on the first Prelude of Bach)](#p8) | piano and violin, the tune on the strings | every evening | yes |
| 3 | [Clair de lune](#p9) | piano alone, the tune on the piano | every evening |  |

### The title music, and everything else

- **Title music:** [Daphnis et Chloe: Lever du jour](#p113) (src/title_music.jo): 19 bars, about 77 s, with a gain curve after the receiver.
- **Café Aman** is a radio station (1360 kHz, 21:00–05:00 local), not a place in the game: plucked strings, tangos round midnight.
- **Street musicians** play a generated plucked phrase (src/street_phrase.jo: a scale, a theme and its variations on a bouzouki part), not a catalogue piece; only the nearest musician is heard (src/life_audio.jo).
- **Scenarios:** no scenario cue uses a catalogue piece (the only users of `MUSIC_PIECES` are the radio, the hotel band, the title and the debug menu's audition list).
- **The announcer, Morse, the engine and the ambience** are not music and are not listed.

## Adding a piece

To put a new piece on the page, add a row with the status `requested`: a work, its composer, and anything you know (a year, a link, why). Either:

- run `python3 tools/music_status.py --add "Composer; Work; year; a note or link"` (year, note and link are optional), which appends the row to `requested` in `data/music/status-notes.json` and rewrites this page; or
- edit `data/music/status-notes.json` yourself: add an object `{"composer": "...", "work": "...", "year": "...", "source": "...", "note": "..."}` to `requested`, then run `python3 tools/music_status.py`.

An agent researching it changes `status` (to wanted, source found, blocked or not planned) and fills `source` and `note` in the same row; when the piece enters the catalogue (tools/music_pack.py `PIECES`, then `python3 tools/music_pack.py`) its row moves to the pieces' notes (`pieces`, keyed by catalogue id) and, if it is on the LOGH list, its list row gains its `pieces`. The rest of the page is regenerated from the repository by `python3 tools/music_status.py`; `tests/music_status_test.py` fails when the page is out of date. A piece not public domain needs the user's explicit approval before anything is committed (see the rule above).

## Gaps

Fields that could not be determined are marked `?` on the page. They are:

- Which movements the Water Music arrangement (#73), the Handel Oboe Concerto (#75) and Mozart's "Jupiter" (#80) hold: not recorded in data/music/SOURCES.md; read them from the source files.
- Whether the staged CC0 PDMX rows (about 128, in scratch) include a usable transcription of any of the scan-only (blocked on OMR) LOGH works: only the pieces proposed for the radio were searched.
- Haydn symphonies 8 and 81, Mozart symphony 1 and Mozart piano sonata 17 were not in the earlier research: no source, edition or publication date looked up.
- George Frideric Handel, Concerto for trumpet, strings and continuo (attribution/catalogue number unconfirmed): year
- George Frideric Handel, Six-movement piece for harp and orchestra (original Japanese soundtrack title needs clarification): year
- Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Piano Sonata No. 17 (numbering varies; work identification should be checked): year
- Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Unidentified Adagio, Largo–Allegro and other fragments (not counted as distinct confirmed works): year
